edits.old: We identify the extra smoothness explicitly: the local Bergman sums have no common zeros and are smooth and positive; the glued potential is the logarithm of a finite sum of these smooth positive sums with smooth cutoff factors. At every point at least one cutoff is positive. The logarithm is therefore smooth. This is the construction preceding \cite[Theorem 14.12]{DemAM11}; the smooth remainder after resolution is also recorded there in (14.14). Smoothness here follows from the construction with unit ideals, not merely from having bounded analytic type. The displayed smooth forms represent the same closed class and satisfy its defining nef estimates.
edits.new: These are closed representatives of $\{R\}_{\mathrm{BC}}$. Given any $\epsilon>0$, choose $j$ with $\epsilon_j\leq\epsilon$. This is the defining nef estimate.

edits.old: Repeat the unit-ideal regularization argument of \cref{lem:bounded-closed-potential-nef}. Its curvature estimate allows the arbitrary smooth lower bound $-\beta$, and therefore gives smooth $v_j$ with $\beta+\ddc v_j\geq-\epsilon_j\gamma$, $\epsilon_j\to0$. Each form has derivative $\pi^*\mathrm{d}\theta$ and represents the same affine class. This proves nefness in the stated affine sense; closedness played no role in this estimate.
edits.new: Apply \cref{prop:bounded-almost-regularization} to $v$ in the smooth background $\beta$. It gives smooth $v_j$ with $\beta+\ddc v_j\geq-\epsilon_j\gamma$, $\epsilon_j\downarrow0$. These forms represent the same affine class and have exterior derivative $\pi^*\mathrm{d}\theta$, proving nefness. The regularization proposition requires no closedness of $\beta$.
